title: How BuildKit builds
dek: BuildKit never executes a Dockerfile. This third part of a four-part Docker teardown follows docker build from the CLI's argv rewrite into buildx and over gRPC into the BuildKit inside dockerd, compiles a Dockerfile into LLB, re-derives three vertex digests of alpine:latest's real build byte for byte from its published provenance, takes the solver's two cache keys apart to show why a comment or a touch keeps the cache and a chmod busts it, watches the daemon pull the build context from the client, and ends at the exporters, the cache formats and the attestations a build writes.
byline: 23 October 2026 · Subject: buildkit@f5b59a1f (v0.34.1, inside Docker Engine 29.9.2) · Part 3 of 4 · Read from the source and the specs; measured where this machine allows
description: Docker Engine 29.9.2 and BuildKit v0.34.1 taken apart, part 3: docker build as buildx over gRPC, the Dockerfile frontend and # syntax=, LLB as a protobuf Merkle DAG reproduced from alpine's provenance, the solver's fast and slow cache keys, context transfer, RUN mounts and the runc executor, and exporters, cache export and attestations.
og_description: Part 3 of a four-part Docker teardown at BuildKit v0.34.1 (f5b59a1f) inside Engine 29.9.2: docker build rewritten into buildx, gRPC on the API socket, a three-stage Dockerfile compiler, alpine:latest's three LLB vertex digests recomputed from 75-, 172- and 246-byte protobufs, a cache key that drops mtime, proxy env and secret values, a context the daemon pulls from the client, RUN steps exec'd straight into runc, and the index, cache and provenance a build exports.
twitter_description: BuildKit v0.34.1 taken apart: Dockerfile to LLB, vertex digests reproduced byte for byte, the two cache keys, context transfer, RUN via runc, exporters and attestations.
